overview: This bill aims to speed up federal permits for certain critical minerals projects backed by the Defense Department. In 2022 the President authorized the Defense Department to use the Defense Production Act, a law that lets the government support production of materials needed for national defense, to boost U.S. mining and processing of minerals used in items such as batteries. The bill would automatically treat these Defense-backed projects, such as mine feasibility studies, recovering minerals from mine waste, and modernizing processing plants, as "covered projects" under the FAST-41 program, which provides coordinated federal reviews and set timelines, and would list them on the public online Permitting Dashboard that tracks review progress. A project's sponsor could ask to be left out. As of June 9, 2026, a House committee had approved it and it was awaiting a vote by the full House.
for: Supporters say faster, more predictable permitting for domestic mineral projects helps reduce U.S. reliance on foreign supply chains for materials vital to defense and technology.
against: Critics say automatically placing these projects on a fast track, skipping the usual eligibility requirements, could pressure agencies to rush environmental and community reviews of mining projects.
